fail: Fail if the view is only black, white and gray, with no color ground anywhere.
Fail if any item is shown without its photo, or its photo is not the largest image in its group.
Fail if the second most likely action is not an outline, or a side action such as Change or Message is not a gray fill.
Fail if something that asks for a decision offers two actions or fewer, counting what is under More.
Fail if a sentence explains what the screen could show, or a label could be cut and the screen still be understood.
Fail if you can't name the shipped app that does this job the same way.
Fail if Sell lists items as rows of text in place of a grid of photos with small state pills.
Fail if a feed is boxed cards in place of ruled rows with room, or a notice is not in a card with an x to dismiss it. The item in a feed is open again as R29.
Fail if the state on a photo is a solid block in place of a soft corner tag, or its word and icon are hard to read over the photo.
Fail if the gradient sits on more than one thing at rest, or a sale does not fill the whole screen with it, with a haptic and a sound.
Fail if the gradient is a still picture. It drifts slowly and is barely noticed.
Fail if the selected tab is shown by anything but the filled icon in ink, has a line, dot or pill under it, or its label is a different weight from the other tabs.
Fail if a photo that opens a page does not grow into it, or a button gives nothing back the moment it is pressed.
Fail if a gradient is not three neighboring hues on the ring. The named set is open as R17.
Fail if Clofie sets a number or words a person wrote, or anything beyond the wordmark, a screen title and the headline of a moment.
Fail if a gradient is a picture file in place of code, or one gradient cuts to the next in place of changing into it.
Fail if the black pill sits flat with no faint glow under it, or the glow is strong enough to notice first.
Fail if live is any color but sky, sold any color but mint, or needs you any color but marigold.
Fail if a tint sits on gray, a fill and a line share one edge, a photo has no 1 px inner edge, or aqua or peach marks a state or a kind of thing.
Fail if the sum of what you keep is not a paper slip with dotted leaders and a torn foot.
Fail if a sale plays any sound but a finger snap, or plays it without the haptic. Which snap is open as R36.
Fail if a notice card is any color but gray, or marigold tint when it needs the person.
Fail if Clofie appears on a card headline or an amount.
Fail if a label in a button, tag, chip or tab sits more than 1 px above or below the middle of its control, measured from its cap height to its baseline.
Fail if the padding at the icon end of a pill is not one step less than at its text end, or a tag's icon is not the same distance from the top, the bottom and the near end.
Fail if a card's gradient has a deadline and is at full strength two days out or pale in its last hour, if it pulses or visibly animates its strength, or if the countdown words are missing.
Fail if a stuck listing's photo loses its color, a standing other than Hot or Stuck gets a color, or Hot shows without the fact that earned it.
Fail if the gradient sits on a card other than the first one that needs the person (a decision with a clock, nearest deadline first), or on a failed or news card.

rule: One image, one fresh call. One agent never makes all three designs.
A prompt gives the intention and how it will be judged, never the content, the numbers or a rule doc.
A screen is built only from the parts in app/src/ui, and separators come from the parts.
Every value comes from brand/tokens.css.
The behavior table is written before the behavior.
Everything that runs logs through log/.
Skip the image model when the parts that exist can build the screen.
fail: Fail if an image round was run for a screen that the parts in app/src/ui and the brand values could already build.

rule: The fixed surroundings go into every design prompt as images.
fail: Fail if a design changes or leaves out what is fixed around it: the tab bar, the header, the wordmark.

rule: Tests come from the behavior table, from an agent that is not the builder, and fail before the code exists.
fail: Fail if a control's behavior was built before a test for its row failed, or the builder edited the table or the test.

rule: At most three image rounds, and stop when a round brings no new accepted finding.
fail: Fail if a fourth image round ran, or the latest design was carried forward in place of the best so far.

rule: The same job looks and moves the same on every screen.
fail: Fail if this screen does a job another screen already does, with a different part, look or motion.

rule: Space says what belongs together, and every gap has a reason.
fail: Fail if two gaps are equal where one separates parts of a thing and the other separates things, or you can't say why a gap is the size it is.

rule: Ideation makes 2 to 4 designs. In the first round each leans toward one person; in later rounds one or two are pushed on one lever.
fail: Fail if a design call was given two steers (two people, two levers, or a person and a lever), or a first-round design was given no person.

rule: A persona line gives the situation, never the screen.
fail: Fail if the line that leans a design toward a person names a layout, a component or copy, in place of who is looking and what they want.

rule: The judge says how and why each design serves its person.
fail: Fail if the judgment of a first-round design does not name which element answers which want of its person, what that costs another person, and whether that want is sourced or only named in product/personas.md.

rule: The merge keeps what serves one person and costs nobody.
fail: Fail if the merged design drops something a person needed without saying so, averages the designs into one that serves nobody, or serves the reseller at the cost of someone clearing out.

rule: A large screen or a section of the signed-out site makes one bold move.
fail: Fail if you cannot name in one sentence the one way a large screen, or a section of the signed-out site, departs from how apps of this kind do it.

rule: A bold move or a motion names its purpose.
fail: Fail if a bold move or a motion cannot name what it is for: what to look at first, the story, feedback, a change of state, or recognition. It looked good is not a purpose.

rule: The bold move is ownable.
fail: Fail if the screen or page could belong to another product once the wordmark is covered.

rule: One bold move per view.
fail: Fail if an app view makes more than one bold move, a site section more than one, or a page has more than one signature motion.

rule: A bold move never breaks the basics.
fail: Fail if a bold move hurts legibility, changes the size, place or behavior of a familiar control, or takes first place from the item photo.

rule: Reduce Motion is never overridden.
A screen never sets a raw duration.
No scroll listeners and no transition: all.
Every named motion has a reason.
A photo has a faint inner edge.
fail: Fail if a photo with a white or pale edge bleeds into the page because it has no 1 px inner edge.

rule: Fixed-width digits only where amounts line up or change.
fail: Fail if amounts in a column or an amount that updates in place use digits of uneven width, or fixed-width digits are used in running text.

rule: Shapes are centered by eye.
fail: Fail if an icon or a glyph in a button or a circle looks off center, such as a play triangle or an arrow sitting to one side.

rule: Headlines break evenly.
fail: Fail if a headline of two lines or more leaves one short word alone on its last line.

rule: Words on a screen use the curly apostrophe and the ellipsis character.

fail: Fail if a shape, line, icon, image or block of color carries no item, amount, state, word or action. Name it.
Fail if the first thing you see with your eyes half shut is not an item photo, an amount of money or the app's own screen, unless the view is a title, an end card or an icon.
Fail if a number appears that a stranger could not explain from the words beside it.

Fail if it makes the same choice as the no-brand default handed over with the render on three or more of: palette, type, layout grid, card shape, icon style, copy pattern, image style. With no default handed over, say so and skip this line.

rule: Items are real photos.
fail: Fail if an item is drawn, rendered in 3D or shown in a lifestyle scene, in place of a real photo of the thing on a plain ground in daylight.

rule: One idea per slide or panel.
fail: Fail if you can't say what a slide or panel is for in five words, or it makes two points.

rule: The app is shown as it is.
fail: Fail if an app screen is tilted, reflected, held in a hand, redrawn, or so small its text can't be read.

rule: A line belongs to secondhand.
fail: Fail if a line promises a benefit and names no item, amount, marketplace or step of the product. Quote it.

rule: The field is behind the one thing that matters.
fail: Fail if the gradient sits behind anything but the most important thing in the view, or behind more than a few words.

rule: Nothing is invented.
fail: Fail if a number about the market, users or results, or a quoted person, has no source named in the view or in the notes handed over, or a made-up value is not marked as a demo. Quote it.

rule: One point per view, said as a sentence a stranger gets in 3 seconds.
fail: Fail if a heading is a topic label with no verb ("The problem", "Our solution", "What it does"), a view makes two points, or you could not say the view's point after looking for 3 seconds. Quote the heading.

rule: A claim sits beside its proof.
fail: Fail if a view claims something about the product or the market and nothing in the same view proves it: the real screen, the real item, or a number with its source. Fail if a statistic comes before any one specific case. Quote the claim.

rule: Nothing is there for decoration.
fail: Fail if taking away a picture, an icon, a shape or a line of text would leave the view's point unchanged. Name what to take away.

rule: A label sits next to its thing, and a slide is not the script.
fail: Fail if a label is apart from what it names (a legend, a key, a footnote across the view), or the words on a slide are full sentences the speaker would say aloud.

rule: Whatever acts looks pressable, and nothing else does.
fail: Fail if a row or notice that opens a screen has no chevron, a decision card that opens its item lacks the depth of brand Art. 9, a tag, count or countdown looks pressable, or a dismiss X is the only control on something that needs an action.

rule: A countdown shows only a real deadline, calmly.
fail: Fail if a countdown shows a time the card's data does not carry as a deadline (site expiry, ship-by, pickup, the Decision's expiry), ticks by the second, is red or pulses, or shows hours past 24 instead of a day and time.

rule: A decision card names its kind before its title, and carries its own deadline.
fail: Fail if a decision card has no tag with a word and an icon above its title, or its deadline sits in a separate banner instead of on the card.

rule: No state by hue alone, and no brown in dark.
fail: Fail if a state is told apart only by color, or a dark ground has OKLCH hue 70 to 115 with L under .5.

rule: Nothing sits in a corner's curve.
fail: Fail if text or an icon in a rounded box's corner comes closer to the curved edge than the box's padding, measured on the ink: on a decision card with radius 36 and padding 16, a top-right countdown under 24 from the right edge fails. Content concentric with the box passes.

rule: A site's logo is its saved square icon.
source: Ben, 03:49 (product/words.md): "you should always use the icdons you grabbed"; ledger L17

rule: A state never moves things.
source: Ben, 03:49 (product/words.md): "when the gray box is there, things are moving over"
